rows: Severe thunderstorm winds damaged the roofs of homes in Carrizo Springs.

Severe thunderstorm winds struck from west of Carrizo Springs into Maverick County. As the storms moved southward, they knocked over trees and blew down power lines from west of Carrizo Springs to El Indio and southward to the Aerostat site.
Severe thunderstorm winds blew down trees and power lines in the Carrizo Springs area. The winds also damaged roofs in the city.
The Circle V Ranch center in Carrizo reported nickel size hail in Asherton.
Nickel size hail fell at a ranch along Highway 277.
There were also reports of trees down near Brundage.
There was nickel to golfball size hail reported at the Briscoes Catarina Ranch.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 50 mph which knocked down power lines and caused minor damage to a house.

A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 58 mph that produced widespread damage in Carrizo Springs. A number of roofs and walls were damaged and a number of trees and telephone poles were knocked down.
Quarter size hail was reported by the public.
Public report of hail larger than golf balls just outside of Big Wells via Twitter.
A thunderstorm produced half dollar size hail north of Catarina.
A thunderstorm produced baseball size hail at a convenience store in Catarina.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that blew down some large trees and damaged fences and outdoor structures in Asherton.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that snapped power poles and damaged a business sign on Hwy 277 in Carrizo Springs.
A thunderstorm produced hail up to quarter size at the intersection of US 83 and US 277 in Carrizo Springs.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that snapped 3-6 inch diameter tree limbs in Carrizo Springs near the intersection of US 83 and US 277.
A thunderstorm produced wind gusts estimated at 70 mph that damaged the front porch of a house and bent a metal post in Carrizo Springs.
